clue.text: Action ending with defeat in bomb-proof chamber

parts.note: a case is a legal action brought in court
checkmate, or mate, is the move that ends a chess game in defeat

explanation.surface: A battle that ends in a loss takes place inside a shelter built to withstand bombs.
explanation.definitionFit: A casemate is an armoured, shell-proof vault in a fortification or warship from which guns are fired.

clue.text: The boatman's tea boy

parts.note: cha is British slang for tea
Ron is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A ferryman has a lad who brings him his tea.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Charon ferries the dead across the river Styx.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Charon is the ferryman who rows the dead to the underworld.

clue.text: Trace crime by ploughman, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a sin is a crime and a tiller is one who tills the land, a ploughman

explanation.surface: Investigators follow the trail of an offence committed by a farmhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trace' looks like a verb about tracking down the crime; it is the noun meaning a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is the tiniest particle, a trace or hint of something.

clue.text: In Virgil Latin is the great teacher

indicators.note: the Latin verb goes inside the poet's name

parts.note: Publius Vergilius Maro was Virgil's full name
est is Latin for is

explanation.surface: Virgil's Latin is held up as the work of a supreme instructor.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgil's cognomen Maro is the piece needed, not the usual name.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master, a distinguished teacher or conductor of music.

clue.text: Claim the championship

definitions.meaning: a claim is a right or entitlement to something
the champion's status in a sport, the crown

explanation.definitionFit: A title is both a legal right to property and the status of champion in a sport.

clue.text: Loves the fuss about Society

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother, as in much ado about nothing
re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone delights in the commotion surrounding high society.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to be deeply fond of them, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Such currency is claimed to be free

indicators.note: letters set free are loosened from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A form of money is said to cost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claimed' looks like 'is said'; it is the fodder whose letters are freed.
explanation.definitionFit: Decimal currency is money divided into units of tens, as Britain adopted in 1971.

clue.text: Run over party piece

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
on means over or on top of
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A performer runs through their party piece once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party piece' looks like one phrase but splits: party gives DO and piece is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical composition or movement with a recurring main theme.

clue.text: Boy is placed in disgrace in an unforgiving way

indicators.note: the boy's name is put inside the word for disgrace

parts.note: to sully is to disgrace or tarnish
Len is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad is shamed and treated harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sullenly means in a sulky, resentful manner, unwilling to forgive.

clue.text: With Vat, tyres can be a ridiculous figure

indicators.note: the letters can be made into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: With VAT added, the price of tyres becomes absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is Britain's sales tax; here it is just letters for the anagram signalled by 'can be'.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque, absurd imitation or caricature.

clue.text: Any tall American can construct a food tube

indicators.note: to construct is to build from parts, so the letters of the three words are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A lanky American is apparently able to build a pipe for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can construct' looks like the American doing the building, but it is the anagram signal applied to all fifteen letters of 'Any tall American'.
explanation.definitionFit: The digestive passage running from mouth to anus is the tube through which food travels.

clue.text: More than half a sonnet written for musicians

definitions.meaning: a sonnet has fourteen lines, and its opening group of eight is called by this name
a group of eight performers playing together

explanation.definitionFit: Eight is more than half of fourteen sonnet lines, and an eight-player ensemble carries the same name, here in its French-style spelling.

clue.text: Leave hurriedly in vessel keeping low

indicators.note: the vessel holds another word inside it, as a container keeps its contents

parts.note: a vase is a vessel for flowers
to low is to moo, the sound cattle make

explanation.surface: Someone is told to clear off while inside a ship that stays near the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' reads as an adjective about the vessel, but it is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Vamoose is American slang, from Spanish, meaning to get out fast.

clue.text: Slips into baggy trousers

definitions.meaning: loose knee-length drawers once worn by women, named after Amelia Bloomer

explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are both clumsy mistakes in British slang and an old style of loose women's knickers.

clue.text: This shows who the title-holder is

definitions.text: This shows who the title-holder is

parts.words: This shows who the title-holder is
parts.note: title-holder suggests a champion, but here it is the owner of a book, named on a label pasted inside

explanation.definitionFit: Ex libris, Latin for from the books of, is a bookplate naming the volume's owner.

clue.text: Laboratory has origins of English language to identify

indicators.note: the origins of words are their beginnings, so take the opening letter of each

explanation.surface: A research lab draws on the roots of the English tongue to name things.
explanation.definitionFit: To label something is to tag it with a name so it can be recognised.

clue.text: Model for an obscene publication

parts.note: blue means smutty or obscene, as in a blue film
print is published matter

explanation.surface: Someone poses for a dirty magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as someone posing; it means a plan or template.
explanation.definitionFit: A blueprint is a detailed design or template serving as a pattern.

clue.text: Part of gun carriage raised in exercise

parts.note: a limber is the detachable front part of a gun carriage
up means raised or lifted

explanation.surface: A section of artillery carriage is lifted during military drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; 'exercise' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To limber up is to warm up the muscles with stretching before exercise.

clue.text: Likeness that's out of a periodical

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is stands outside the periodical, wrapping round it

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
mag is short for magazine, a periodical publication

explanation.surface: A picture is said to have been taken from a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' reads as taken from a magazine, but it means one piece standing outside another; i.e. is Latin id est, that is.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or representation that resembles its subject.

clue.text: Old metal weight, now obsolete

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
tin is a metal
ct is the abbreviation for carat, a unit of weight for gems

explanation.surface: A metal weight from the past is no longer in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Extinct means having died out, no longer existing or used.

clue.text: Belabour tramp

definitions.meaning: to belabour is to attack someone with blows, phrased as a two-word verb
a tramp here is an idle loafer who avoids work

explanation.definitionFit: To lay about someone is to hit out wildly, a beating; and as one word it names a lazy idler or vagrant.

clue.text: Fortification for conflict en masse

indicators.note: en is French for in, so the conflict goes inside the mass

parts.note: masse is French for mass, and bulk means mass
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: Defences are built for a battle fought by the whole population.
explanation.walkthrough: 'en masse' looks like one French phrase meaning all together, but it splits: 'en' is French for in, the container signal, and 'masse' is French for mass.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulwark is a defensive wall or rampart.

clue.text: Girl will accept nothing as a gratuity

indicators.note: the girl's name takes in the letter, accepting it within

parts.note: Bunty is a girl's name, also a British girls' comic
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A girl takes nothing as a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A bounty is a generous gift or reward, like a tip.

clue.text: It's hot in the club bar — turn to this sort of gin

indicators.note: the letter for hot is placed inside the following words, as the clue says it goes in them

parts.note: a bat is the club used in cricket or baseball

indicators.note: the word for bar is turned round to be read backwards

parts.note: but means except, as bar does in all bar one
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: In a heated clubhouse bar, someone switches to a rough kind of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses BUT (bar, meaning except) to TUB; H for hot goes into BAT + TUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathtub gin was cheap homemade spirit, notoriously mixed in baths during American Prohibition.

clue.text: Showing poor taste — and a bit wet

definitions.meaning: slightly sticky, as fresh paint is before it dries

explanation.definitionFit: Tacky means both tasteless and kitsch, and slightly sticky because not yet dry.

clue.text: W Indian dance company accepts odd plays

indicators.note: the company takes something in, holding it between its letters
odd means strange or irregular, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe takes on some strange scripts to stage a Caribbean dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Calypso is a Caribbean, specifically Trinidadian, style of song and its associated dance.

clue.text: Satchel a pupil holds

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them, spanning the space between

explanation.surface: A schoolchild carries a bag for books.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism a chela is a disciple or student of a guru.

clue.text: Tory party taken in about the dole and having second thoughts

indicators.note: the Tory party is enclosed by the outer words, taken in by them

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a dole is a portion handed out, a ration
Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party
a side is one party in a contest or dispute

explanation.surface: A Conservative faction sinks to claiming unemployment benefit and starts to rethink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the dole' suggests British unemployment benefit, but here it is a ration doled out.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the act of thinking again about a decision, which matches having second thoughts as a gerund phrase.

clue.text: This cactus is a drug on the market

definitions.text: This cactus is a drug on the market

parts.words: This cactus is a drug on the market
parts.note: a drug on the market is an idiom for goods nobody wants, but this Mexican cactus is literally sold as a hallucinogen

explanation.definitionFit: Peyote is a small spineless Mexican cactus whose buttons contain the hallucinogen mescaline.

clue.text: Favour tarry rope for mast

parts.note: to back someone is to favour or support them
to tarry is to linger or stay

explanation.surface: Someone prefers a tar-coated line for securing a ship's mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tarry' reads as covered in tar; it is the verb to linger.
explanation.definitionFit: A backstay is a rope or cable running from a masthead aft to brace it.
